- When sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for early periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), model tends to ignore it; apply downward bias of 1–4% for 3–7 days ahead.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.20), model often overreacts and forecasts too high; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak or adjust using sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates downward trends; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent 5-day average is falling.
- If sentiment history shows no change (all 0.00), model should not assume momentum; use 10-day moving average as baseline for correction.
